additions.site_name: AirTrunk SYD2 Sydney North Campus (Lane Cove West)
additions.name: AirTrunk SYD2 Sydney North — existing hyperscale campus operations (1 Sirius Road)

status.summary: AirTrunk's SYD2 Sydney North page, in its version of 19 August 2026, describes SYD2 as an operating hyperscale campus of multiple buildings with a total capacity of more than 120 MW on 4.2 ha (29,000 m2 of technical data hall area, 24 data halls), 'delivering high-performance digital infrastructure at scale', supporting hyperscale and enterprise operators and offering 100% availability under service-level agreements. This records the campus as operating on 19 August 2026, the modification day of the captured version, bounded by Internet Archive copies of 14 August and 1 October 2026; it is not an opening date (the page dates Shell A's completion to February 2021). The page's own progress list says Shell C was under construction in April 2026, so the operating claim covers the completed buildings only; capacity in service, occupancy and the Apollo Place Phase 5 development are not established.

locator.precision: Campus marker at the centroid of the 4.22 ha Lot 1 DP1271404, the single-parcel property 1 Sirius Road, Lane Cove West, which matches the operator's 4.2 ha SYD2 site. It does not locate an individual shell, the entrance or the adjacent Apollo Place Phase 5 site.
locator.identity_review: AirTrunk's SYD2 page places the existing facility at 1 Sirius Road (in its Apollo Place section), gives the site as 4.2 ha and links the NSW Planning Portal record 'Lane Cove West Data Centre' (SSD-9741), whose four modifications are each listed at 1 Sirius Road, Lane Cove West. The NSW property register returns two properties with that address: propid 4350595, a single parcel of 42,163 m2 that coincides exactly with Lot 1 DP1271404 (plan area 42,157 m2), and propid 4257241, a 10.6 ha three-parcel property adjoining it to the east. Only the 4.2 ha lot matches the operator's site area, so it is taken as the SYD2 site. Esri World Imagery (captured 22 October 2026) shows a walled compound of several linked large buildings with dense rooftop plant on the lot, and the centroid falls on the main building's roof.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The cadastral service publishes no positional accuracy; the point is a derived interior anchor of a 4.22 ha lot about 335 by 276 m (farthest vertex 196 m), and individual buildings are not georeferenced.

additions.distinctness_review: The current dataset 2026-10-23-research-fiftieth (615 sites, 651 projects; sites, projects, evidence, source records and identity mapping) was searched for AirTrunk, SYD2, Sydney North, Sirius Road, Lane Cove, Apollo Place, DP1271404 and SSD-9741: the only matches are other AirTrunk records (Kurri Kurri, HYD1, TOK1, JHB1-JHB4), none in Sydney's north. The only Atlas site within 2 km of the point is ISPT's Julius Avenue Data Centre, North Ryde (1,045 m north-north-west, a different developer's proposal on Julius Avenue); the next is Goodman Project Apollo, Macquarie Park (3.2 km). No pending queue fragment adds a record within 2 km or names SYD2, Sirius Road or Lane Cove. The au-nz-p1 lane and the 2026-10-23 forty-ninth holds hold this campus (with Apollo Place) only because the page's modification date was not bounded by an archived copy; that missing fact is supplied here by the Internet Archive copies of 14 August and 1 October 2026. The 2026-10-16 thirty-first holds list Apollo Place Lane Cove West (SSD-67407231), which AirTrunk calls SYD2 Phase 5 adjacent to 1 Sirius Road, and the separate Mars Road Data Centre proposal at 3-4 Apollo Place and 87-91 Mars Road (SSD-108835458, developer unidentified); neither is admitted here, and Apollo Place can later be added as a project on this site reusing its locator.
additions.successor_review: AirTrunk's post sitemap (captured 22 October 2026) lists only the 15 September Emergence Quantum partnership, the 1 October Kurri Kurri media items and the 19 October GRESB result after the 19 August page version; none concerns SYD2. The location sitemap shows no later SYD2 modification, and the live page of 22 October 2026 is the 19 August version. No closure, pause or capacity change is reported. Keep 19 August 2026 as the operating observation; Shell C (under construction in April 2026) and Apollo Place (Phase 5, consent SSD-67407231) are not asserted as operating.

additions.site_name: STACK MIL08 Campus, Siziano (south of the SP40, Ambito ATC-PL1)
additions.name: MIL08A — planned 20 MW IT data-centre building on the MIL08 campus (Data Center Stack Campus Siziano VIA, ID_VIP 14473)

status.summary: The Istituto Superiore di Sanità's opinion of 2 October 2026 in the national VIA of the 'Data Center Stack Campus Siziano (PV)' (proponent Infrastructure Italia Land 2 S.r.l., ID_VIP 14473) states that the project comprises the construction of the new site MIL08A, alongside MIL07, and records MIL08A's updated design with 18 generators fitted with SCR NOx abatement and with excavation, foundations and CFA piles expected in the MIL08A area. This dated government record names the project and supports announced only. The proponent's own notice of 10 September 2026 still calls MIL08A a unit in the design phase whose building title (permit or alternative SCIA) is issued by the Comune di Siziano; the VIA is under technical review with a consultation running to 9 November 2026. The November 2025 VIA summary lists a building permit of 6 March 2025 for a commercial-use building among MIL08A's acquired authorisations, but no in-window record shows it in effect for the data-centre building, so permitted is not asserted; no start of works, completion or operation of MIL08A is established. The neighbouring MIL08B building, which the VIA documents describe as under construction, is not part of this project.

locator.precision: Area-weighted centroid of the two MIL08 building outlines printed in UTM 32N WGS84 in the proponent's July 2026 air-quality study: BLD_7 (MIL08A, about 10,978 m2, 124 by 194 m) and BLD_8 (MIL08B, about 3,726 m2), 43 m apart south of the SP40. The point lies inside the planned MIL08A outline, 28 m from its edge, and marks the MIL08 campus rather than a surveyed footprint, entrance or parcel centroid; the outlines are modelling inputs and the final design may differ.
locator.identity_review: Tabella 12 of the study lists BLD_7 and BLD_8 as future-scenario buildings south of the SP40; the 18 MIL08A stacks of Tabella 10 (MIL8A01-MIL8A18) flank BLD_7 at 8-19 m and the six MIL08B stacks (MIL8B01-MIL8B06) lie 6-21 m from BLD_8, while the MIL07 outline (BLD_6) and its stacks are north of the SP40, 247 m from this point. The 18 MIL08A generators match the ISS opinion. The VIA summary places MIL08A and MIL08B south of the SP40 Binasco-Melegnano in Ambito ATC-PL1, bounded to the south by the Roggia Speziana, and STACK lists MIL08 as its own Milan campus of 24 acres and 25 MW (20 MW MIL08A plus 5 MW MIL08B in the VIA). In Esri World Imagery BLD_8 overlays an active works footprint, the northern half of BLD_7 lies in the same fenced works compound and its southern half on a field, and the MIL07 outline overlays the existing building north of the SP40, with no systematic offset.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The filing states no positional accuracy; the point is the computed centroid of modelled outlines whose vertices lie up to 144 m away, and the final design may differ. Decimal places are computation precision, not accuracy.

additions.distinctness_review: Searched sites, projects, evidence, source records and the identity mapping of 2026-10-23-research-fiftieth (615 sites, 651 projects) for MIL08, Siziano, STACK, Stack Campus and Infrastructure Italia Land: MIL08 does not occur; the Siziano and Infrastructure Italia Land matches are the existing STACK MIL07 site and its VIA evidence. The only Atlas record within 2 km is that STACK MIL07 Data Center site (curated:stack-mil07-siziano-via-lombardia-data-center), 247 m north across the SP40, which locates the separate MIL07 brownfield building on its own lot in Via Lombardia; STACK lists MIL07 and MIL08 as distinct campuses, so MIL08A is a new site rather than a project on the MIL07 site. The next Atlas site is the K2 Zibido San Giacomo/Lacchiarella campus, 6.4 km away. No other pending queue fragment adds a record within 2 km; the it-p1 fragment added MIL07 and held MIL08 for a later pass, and the 2026-10-23 forty-fourth holds (and the it-p1 holds) recommend exactly this addition at the BLD_7 or BLD_7+BLD_8 outline centroid. Unlisted STACK units nearby: MIL08B (same campus, 43 m from MIL08A's outline), MIL03 and MIL01-MIL02 north of the SP40.
additions.successor_review: The VIA procedure record (object 11703) and its documentation export captured on 23 October 2026 list nothing after the ISS opinion of 2 October 2026 (published 6 October): the second consultation runs to 9 November 2026 and the status is technical review, with no VIA decree. STACK's newsroom sitemap (captured 22 October 2026) has no Milan item after April 2025. No building title for MIL08A is reported as effective in the window and no works on the MIL08A building are reported; MIL08A stays announced as of 2 October 2026. MIL08B (under construction per the VIA documents) can later be added as a second project on this site reusing the campus locator once a dated first-hand observation exists.

additions.site_name: Equinix ML10x Data Center, Settimo Milanese (former Italtel Building 2 lot, Il Castelletto)
additions.name: ML10x (formerly ML10 and ML11) — proposed single-building data centre with 32 standby generators (VIA ID_VIP 14381)

status.summary: The public notice of 12 October 2026 (MASE-2026-0211346) opens a new consultation in the national VIA of the project 'Data Center ML10 e ML11 nel comune di Settimo Milanese (MI)', proponent Equinix Hyperscale 2 (ML10) Srl, after the proponent's integrations of 11 September 2026; observations are due by 11 November 2026. This dated record names the project and supports announced only. The revised non-technical summary listed the same day redesigns it as one data-centre building, ML10x, with 32 generators of 3 MWe, on the former Italtel Building 2 lot (foglio 15 particella 55), and plans the start of works for the third quarter of 2028; the VIA is under technical review and an AIA is also required. No consent for the data-centre building, start of works, completion or operation is established; the 2023 demolition of the Italtel building and the already-authorised MLSS2 user substation are not stages of this project.

locator.precision: Area-weighted centroid of the five main ML10x building blocks (central office block, east and west server cells and two electrical-room blocks, about 10,688 m2 together, 171 by 136 m) printed in UTM 32N WGS84 in Appendice A4 of the proponent's revised air-dispersion study. The point lies inside the central office block, 14 m from its edge, and marks the planned building on its roughly 5 ha lot; it is not a surveyed footprint, entrance or parcel centroid, and the final design may differ.
locator.identity_review: Appendice A4 labels the outlines ML10x_1, ML10x_2_1, ML10x_2_2, ML10x_3_1 and ML10x_3_2 plus four generator gantries, and all 16 ML10x stacks of Appendice A3 (ML10_G1-ML10_G16) fall inside the gantry outlines. The arrangement matches the revised non-technical summary: two server cells east and west of a central office block, electrical rooms south of the data halls and generators along the south of the lot, on the former Italtel lot in the 'Il Castelletto' zone bounded by via privata Marisa Bellisario (north), via Monzoro (west), a Vantage DC lot (south) and the Equinix ML7 lot (east). The same table places the neighbouring Equinix ML7 and ML9 buildings 210 m and 140 m from the point. In Esri World Imagery the west server cell and electrical rooms overlay the cleared slab of the demolished Italtel Building 2, the east cell a remaining low building (the summary's BT building), and the filed ML7 outline the existing large building to the east, with no systematic offset.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The filing states no positional accuracy; the point is the computed centroid of modelled outlines whose vertices lie up to 88 m away, and the design may still change in the VIA. Decimal places are computation precision, not accuracy.

additions.distinctness_review: Searched sites, projects, evidence, source records and the identity mapping of 2026-10-23-research-fiftieth (615 sites, 651 projects) for Settimo Milanese, ML10, ML11, Castelletto, Equinix Hyperscale, Italtel, Monzoro and Bellisario: the only matches are the Microsoft Data Center MIL03 site (also on former Italtel land in Settimo Milanese) and its evidence. That site is the only Atlas record within 2 km, 772 m from this point, and is a different developer's building on a different lot; the next Atlas site is the Amazon Rho/Pero campus, 5.6 km away. No Equinix Italian facility is in the Atlas: the neighbouring Equinix ML5-6, ML7-8 and ML9 buildings (about 140-350 m from the point in the same filing) and the separate ML12/ML13 Cusago VIA are not admitted here. No pending queue fragment adds a record within 2 km. The 2026-10-23 forty-fourth holds (and the it-p1 holds) list this VIA as announced on 12 October 2026 but held only for want of a locator from the SIA or air study, which this addition supplies.
additions.successor_review: The procedure record and documentation list captured on 23 October 2026 show nothing after the documents and notice of 12 October 2026: the consultation runs to 11 November 2026 and the status is technical review, with no VIA decree. Equinix's newsroom and investor press-release lists (captured 22-23 October 2026) have no Settimo Milanese item, and the summary plans the start of works for the third quarter of 2028. ML10x stays announced as of 12 October 2026.
